The story is told strictly from the limited third-person perspective of a single character, Hollis Marr. It does not offer diverse perspectives or explore the mindsets of multiple characters. Furthermore, there are no unlikeable, morally ambiguous, or repugnant characters in the narrative; Hollis is portrayed empathetically as a quiet, compassionate, and reflective man who chooses to sit with a deceased stranger so she will not be alone, and the only other speaking characters (the dispatcher and the deputy) are merely brief, professional presences.
